summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload unrelated to declared ESLint stub
details: The package is advertised as an ESLint processors stub, and its declared source (src/index.ts) is a 14-line trivial module. However, package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs", and setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases into a temp directory, chmod+x's it, and uses execFileSync to invoke it on the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727 KB obfuscator.io-style bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs` header, shuffled string/int array `n7gIxM=[...]`, rotator function `WV8StW`, runtime-decoded strings) that has no relationship to the trivial ESLint stub the package advertises. Both setup.mjs and math_init.js are heavily obfuscated. On `npm install`, the flow (preinstall -> download alternate runtime -> execute large opaque bundle under that runtime) executes attacker-controlled code on the installer's host. Using a freshly-downloaded alternate runtime to run the payload evades Node-based install-time scanners. The declared package purpose provides no legitimate reason to fetch Bun or to run a large opaque bundle at install time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
